summary.headline: Aegis Vopak Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12.4% YoY to INR233.8 crore, with liquid terminaling up 31% and operating EBITDA up 15.6% to INR179.4 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 12.4% YoY to INR233.8 crore, led by liquid terminaling (INR126.5 crore, +31% YoY) while gas terminaling fell 3.5% YoY to INR107.2 crore. Operating EBITDA rose 15.6% YoY to INR179.4 crore (about 76.7% margin) and cash PAT was INR124.9 crore. Management said the board approved a 52,000 MT LPG tank at JNPA and 49,577 cbm of liquid capacity at Kochi, and that the Pipavav ammonia terminal (36,000 MT static) was commissioned. Management framed a $5 billion capex plan through FY2030-31, of which about INR10,000 crore is to be commissioned by March/June 2027.

segments.name: Liquid terminaling
segments.commentary: Revenue INR126.5 crore, up 31% YoY, driven by higher volumes, new capacity and product mix; management cited JNPA plot 1 maturing (about INR6,000 realization per unit vs blended INR3,000) and better-located capacity commissioned last year.

segments.name: Gas terminaling
segments.commentary: Revenue INR107.2 crore, down 3.5% YoY on LPG import disruption from the Middle East; management said volumes held up via diversified sourcing and multi-location distribution. Standard throughput rate about INR1,175/MT, INR1,200/MT for some principals.

guidance_outlook: Target to grow volumes at least 25% YoY every year; management said AVTL delivered 3.9 million MT in the last year and expects more than 25% growth.
Liquid capacity to rise from about 1.7 million cbm to about 2.2 million cbm in FY27 and close to 3 million cbm by FY28 end.
About INR10,000 crore of expansion (JNPA, ammonia, liquid) expected to be commissioned by March 2027 or June 2027 at the latest.
Kochi 49,577 cbm expected by early next financial year; CRL4 at Kandla (about 94,148 cbm) targeted for later next year.

Funding: debt gearing capped at 0.6x and debt/EBITDA at 3.5x; about $3 billion of the $5 billion capex to come from debt, with about $2 billion equity net worth target and mandatory dilution to 25% of equity by 2 June 2028.
capex_capacity: JNPA expansion: 318,100 cbm liquid storage, 77,236 MT LPG capacity and a 35,000 MT LPG bottling plant, total outlay INR1,675 crore; first phase of about 100,000 cbm expected in Q3 FY27.
JNPA: board approved a 52,000 MT refrigerated LPG tank; existing liquid capacity about 101,900 cbm.
Kochi: board sanctioned 49,577 cbm; total liquid capacity to reach 132,122 cbm from 82,545 cbm.

Pipavav: 36,000 MT ammonia storage commissioned; 0.5 million MT/yr 15-year take-or-pay petroleum product agreement to start by year-end via additional liquid rail gantry; VLGC-compliant jetty by APM Terminals expected this year; Kandla-Gorakhpur pipeline connection expected in the first half of FY27 (per Q&A, 2-3 months).

Mangalore: 75,000 cbm added last year, total 193,000 cbm; evaluating 60,000 cbm more; LPG rail gantry and bottling investment INR52.5 crore. Haldia: 226,890 cbm liquid storage plus 3 acres of land acquired; Haldia-Panagarh pipeline (HPCL, 60 km) expected October-November 2026.
demand_pricing: LPG throughput is priced per metric ton, not per storage day, and management said there is no escalation; the focus is on volume growth.
Liquid terminaling is charged per cbm capacity, not occupancy, so revenue is not driven by utilization.

Management attributed gas volume resilience to diversified sourcing (ITOCHU partnership, non-Middle East cargoes) and ullage availability; it said domestic LPG shortfall had recovered to about 80-85% of normal by July.
Ammonia realizations described as 2.5-3x LPG realizations; first-year utilization projected at 20-25% of the 36,000 MT static capacity (prorated for an August start).
Pipavav: 15-year take-or-pay with Hindustan Zinc for part of ammonia capacity for its DAP plant.

qa_highlights.question: Are LPG throughput charges fixed by counterparty and term, and why haven't terminal charges risen while distribution margins did?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard rate about INR1,175/MT, INR1,200/MT for some principals; charges are per MT with no escalation. Management said terminaling is infrastructure usage, while distribution margins reflect sourcing and inventory risk during the geopolitical disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AVTL gain share versus national LPG imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited non-Middle East sourcing (none of its ships were stuck), a partner in ITOCHU, and wider distribution using freed-up ullage across more locations than Mumbai and Kandla.

qa_highlights.question: Is 25% volume growth sustainable, and what is the Haldia pipeline impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for at least 25% YoY growth; four pipelines are due this year (Jamnagar-Loni done; Kandla-Gorakhpur at Kandla and Pipavav in 2-3 months; Haldia-Panagarh in 2-3 months). Haldia-Panagarh is HPCL's 60 km line; the Panagarh bottling plant is 0.5 million MT/yr and currently about 0.25 million MT is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and liquid capacity path to FY28, and what is the Pipavav take-or-pay economics?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR10,000 crore to be commissioned by March/June 2027; liquid capacity 1.7 to 2.2 million cbm in FY27 and close to 3 million cbm by FY28 end. The Pipavav 0.5 million MT is higher utilization of existing capacity via rail gantry, not new tankage.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth plans beyond the INR10,000 crore phase and the $5 billion program?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing organic and inorganic options, inland depots, strategic storage and industrial terminals, and said binding agreements will be announced as signed. The $5 billion plan through FY2030-31 is reaffirmed, with timing expected to be lumpy.

qa_highlights.question: Why did liquid revenue jump when capacity did not change?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity added last year was only partly in the base year and has now matured, JNPA plot 1 is fully running, and product mix has changed, which takes time.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a mix of debt and equity, with debt gearing capped at 0.6x and debt/EBITDA at 3.5x, about $3 billion of debt, a $2 billion equity net worth target, and mandatory dilution to 25% by 2 June 2028.

risks_watch: LPG volume trajectory vs the 25% YoY growth target, given Strait of Hormuz disruption and whether non-Middle East sourcing holds if the disruption persists for 1-2 quarters
Commissioning timing slippage on the ~INR10,000 crore phase (JNPA first ~100,000 cbm in Q3 FY27, Kochi 49,577 cbm early next FY, Kandla CRL4 later next year)
Kandla-Gorakhpur and Haldia-Panagarh pipeline timelines (stated as 2-3 months and October-November 2026); Pipavav rail gantry and jetty due by year-end
Funding path to $5 billion capex: debt gearing cap 0.6x, debt/EBITDA 3.5x, mandatory dilution to 25% by 2 June 2028, and the lumpy, unspecified spread of capex beyond INR10,000 crore
Gas segment EBIT pressure: gas revenue fell 3.5% YoY and management did not give gas EBITDA when asked; ammonia first-year utilization of 20-25% is a projection, not a result
key_quotes: So, as you can see, across our businesses, we continue to see multiple growth drivers taking shape.
We like to at least grow in our volumes 25% year-on-year every year. That's our hope.
Occupancy is not what liquid works on. So the rate is on CBM basis.
But these all you cannot time it. It happens, then you just get on with it.
It may be lumpy, it may be simultaneous, time will tell.
summary.management_tone: Confident on liquid growth, JNPA maturity, and the funding plan, but evasive on specifics: it declined to give segment EBITDA (Vopak split) on the call, said the timing of expansion beyond INR10,000 crore cannot be fixed, and deferred strategic storage to government decisions. Cautious on the gas side, attributing the decline to geopolitics while saying volumes held up.
